findings.text: non-blocking: the assertion compares the stored backend against CONFIG["local_backend"], but the fixture sets both default_backend and local_backend to "clive" (line 31), so a regression that dropped the entry's local choice would still record backend "clive" and local true (requests.py:272 sets local=true whenever lane equals local_backend); the lane guard only becomes independent of the value under test when the two names differ.

non-blocking: when an entry asks for the local lane and the configuration declares no local_backend, the guard is skipped so the request is queued on the default backend, while the record written at line 272 reads local=bool(local) and stores local true; the stored request then names a local lane it is not on, where the single-dispatch path records local only when the chosen backend is the configured local_backend (fences.py:238).

non-blocking: a second duration parser _DECLARED_DURATION still matches only one integer-and-unit run, so a request storing the newly accepted "1h30m" reaches _declared_budget_verdict at line 143 and yields budget_seconds None, and an overrun of that budget is judged as having none rather than as duration_over_budget.

non-blocking: _home_snapshot keeps only paths where is_file() is true, so a regression that created an empty run directory under the crew home would leave both the before/after comparison and the list_live() check green, although the done-when says a preview writes no run directory.

non-blocking: the module docstring narrates the defect's history ("On 8 November ... exited 0, printed queued" and "now reaches the batch") rather than stating the mechanism the test guards, which dates the comment against the repository rule that comments are code and not a changelog.
